messages:
maria: Heads-up — I sketched a proposal for trace retention that maps TTL to workload-class instead of just env. want quick feedback before i file a formal RFC.

maria: TL;DR: prod-critical services = hot 14d, prod-standard = warm 60d, non-prod (stage/dev/qa) = cold 30d, archive=365d for compliance-only services. Also per-service token-based cost cap + burst protection.

kenny: +1 on workload-class mapping. env-only stuff breaks when a multi-tenant service handles both critical and low-priority paths.

elaine: curious about sampling implications — do we reduce retention by increasing sampling? we should avoid losing error traces for critical flows.

maria: yep — plan is always: tail-based error sampling (retain 100% of error traces), head-based adaptive sampling for high-volume paths, then apply TTL per workload bucket.

devon: can you paste the config sketch? easier to discuss with concrete example.

maria: sure — rough collector/exporter config snippet:
```yaml
exporters:
  trace_storage:
    rules:
      - service: payments.*
        workload_class: prod-critical
        ttl_days: 14
      - service: api-public.*
        workload_class: prod-standard
        ttl_days: 60
      - env: staging
        workload_class: non-prod
        ttl_days: 30
    archive_after_days: 365
    cost_cap_usd_per_service_per_month: 500
```

kenny: i like the cost cap + per-service. question: where do we enforce cost cap? exporter should emit a throttling metric and the routing layer should drop non-essential spans once cap hit.

elaine: we should also add a label for 'investigate=true' on traces created by trace-alerting so they bypass TTL/cap for a certain window. otherwise postmortem workflows get hamstrung.

devon: operationally, we need a migration plan: existing long-ttl services, how to annotate them? maybe default to current ttl and require owners to opt into shorter buckets.

maria: agreed. proposal: default keep existing TTL for 90 days, then auto-classify by heuristic (qps + error-rate) and put owner on the PR to confirm. owners can request an exception.

kenny: edge-case: high-cardinality debug spans (user ids, device ids) — colder storage still costs if cardinality is bad. we should add an exporter transform to drop high-cardinality attributes unless workload_class == prod-critical.

elaine: yep — transform + scrub policy. also add a small schema audit job that flags when attribute cardinality grows 10x month-over-month.

tracing-bot: archive-run scheduled for 2026-06-05T03:00:00Z — will respect workload_class TTLs on run. :robot_face:

devon: rollout plan idea: start with a single team (payments) for 2 weeks, validate cost delta, query reliability for incident traces, then expand to 5 teams.

maria: action items: (1) i’ll write RFC with config + migration plan, (2) kenny will prototype exporter cost-cap metric & throttling hook, (3) elaine will draft transform rules for attribute scrubbing, (4) devon will run pilot with payments. i'll cc infra and legal for archive retention compliance.

kenny: i'll drop a prototype PR for the exporter this week.

elaine: will draw up the scrub rules and sample diffs.

devon: i'll coordinate payments pilot and get owner list.

maria: cool — thanks all. ping if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
